Hi Chloe,

Thanks for the demo last week — HealthSync is keen to move forward but our security team needs a short package before we start procurement. Specifically they need: 
- Confirmation that customer content will not be used for model training or improvement (company-level non-training commitment).
- A list of subprocessors and a simple description of what data (if any) is persisted by each.
- Evidence that customer prompt/response pairs can be exported (for audit) and that outputs are not considered "shared model improvements."
- Retention window options and the ability to geo-fence storage to US regions.

Can you send a single ZIP or PDF we can circulate internally? Also please indicate how we can opt a customer "out" programmatically (flags, account settings, API call).

Best,
Nadia

Hi Nadia — thanks for outlining the asks. I'm pulling together an "evidence pack" with: a signed DPA amendment template that includes a non-training clause, a current subprocessor CSV export, and an ops note describing our non-training switch and export APIs.

Quick answers:
- Non-training: we enforce a boolean tenant-level flag that prevents any data flows to model improvement pipelines. That flag is enforced at the routing layer and audited.
- Export: customers can export prompt/response logs via the Console or an API endpoint; we will include a sample export and a retention policy table.
- Geo-fence: US-only residency can be enforced for hosted accounts; Dedicated/Private follow customer's infra.

I'll send the pack today and loop legal to propose minimal amendment language.

Regards,

Team — draft language below that legal can include in the amendment; Marcus, please validate the operational assertions so we don't overpromise.

Proposed DPA amendment paragraph (editable):
"Redwood Inference hereby commits that Customer Data, including prompts and generated responses submitted to Redwood services, will not be used to train, fine-tune, or improve Redwood's models or any third-party models, for the duration of the Customer Agreement, unless Customer provides explicit, documented consent. This non-training obligation is enforced by a tenant-level control that prevents forwarding of Customer Data to model improvement pipelines. Redwood will provide evidence of enforcement upon reasonable request, including audit logs and an exportable sample of prompt/response pairs."

Notes/questions for ops:
- How granular is the audit trail (tenant ID, request IDs, timestamps)?
- Do we have a straightforward export sample that can be redacted if needed?
- For US-only residency, what surfaces do we use to enforce it (config + tenant metadata)?

If we can provide a short evidence PDF (1-2 pages) + subprocessor CSV + the amendment doc, that should satisfy HealthSync.

—Aditya

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: aditya.rao@redwood.ai, chloe.martin@redwood.ai, laura.bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 13 Oct 2026 09:06:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Evidence for 'no training' + data handling questions

Confirmed details from infra/ops:
- Non-train enforcement: boolean tenant flag (tenant.no_train = true) enforced at the request gateway. Requests for model-improvement are blocked upstream; we also tag blocked events in the audit log (tenant_id, request_id, timestamp, action=blocked).
- Audit trail: we retain request-level metadata for 90 days by default; we can extend retention to 365 days for an enterprise contract. Exported artifacts contain request_id, prompt hash (SHA256), redaction options, and generated response IDs — we do not include raw secrets in exports.
- Subprocessors: current CSV attached (subprocessors-2026-10.csv). Columns: name, role, country, data_persistence (yes/no), contact.
- Geo-fencing: hosted US residency uses dedicated S3 buckets in us-west-2 and tenant network routing. For HealthSync we can lock exports to US buckets and document the configuration.

I'll produce a concise ops note (single page) plus a sample exported CSV snippet to include in the evidence pack.

—Marcus
